lead.zh-Hans: 我在鱼尾狮旁边，收到了两个方向的招呼。
lead.en: Two greetings met beside the Merlion.

text.zh-Hans: 在新加坡鱼尾狮公园，我和一位旅人约在能看见狮头鱼身的雕像旁碰头。我先朝水声那边挥手，对方却从另一侧走来。我们各说了一声“在这里”，最后笑着站到了同一边。我把这两声记在小纸上，明天想把它们接成一句。
text.en: At Merlion Park in Singapore, a fellow traveler and I had agreed to meet by the lion-headed, fish-bodied statue. I waved toward the splashing water; my companion arrived from the other side. Two calls of “over here” eventually brought us together. I saved both greetings on a slip. Tomorrow they might make one sentence.
Join the two greetings
Remember our meeting directions

lead.zh-Hans: 植物园里，我暂时把句号放进了口袋。
lead.en: My full stop stayed in my pocket at the gardens.

text.zh-Hans: 逛新加坡植物园时，我读到它从1859年走到今天，仍在做植物研究与保护。后来我沿园路慢走，看一片叶影从鞋尖挪开。原本想立刻记下一句话，笔却一直没落下。回去才写了“刚才多站了一会儿”，还特意给它留了个安静的句号。
text.en: At Singapore Botanic Gardens, I read about its beginnings in 1859 and its continuing work in plant research and conservation. Farther along, I stopped as a leaf shadow moved away from my shoes. The pencil waited too. Back at my lodging, the note simply said, “Stayed a little longer.” One quiet full stop seemed enough.
Tell someone about the pause
Notice the shadow beside my shoes

lead.zh-Hans: 鸡饭来了，我的半句话先歇一歇。
lead.en: Chicken rice arrived halfway through my sentence.

text.zh-Hans: 在新加坡吃海南鸡饭，我选了蒸鸡，先尝了带鸡汤香味的米饭。原本要在便纸上写“今天先去”，写到这里，勺子就接了班。吃完再看，半句话像在等我交代午饭。我把鸡饭补在后面，这张小菜单便有了一个有点饿的开头。
text.en: For chicken rice in Singapore, I chose steamed chicken and started with the stock-flavoured rice. My note had reached “Today I first went…” when the spoon took over. After lunch, the unfinished sentence was still waiting. Adding the dish’s name gave my little menu a rather hungry opening.
Finish the interrupted sentence

text.zh-Hans: 比较米饭和鸡肉的香味
text.en: Compare the rice and chicken

lead.zh-Hans: 早餐有一声轻轻的脆响。

text.zh-Hans: 我在新加坡尝了咖椰吐司，烤面包夹着椰子和鸡蛋做的酱。咬下这一份时，轻轻脆了一声；等我想听第二声，已经又吃了一口。我给小菜单写了菜名，再画一个很短的声音记号。它不像乐谱，不过我知道这段早餐从哪里开始。
text.en: My kaya toast in Singapore had coconut-and-egg jam between toasted slices. One bite made a small crunch. By the time I thought of listening again, another bite had disappeared. The menu now has the dish’s name and one tiny sound mark. It will never pass as sheet music, but I know where breakfast began.
Describe the first bite
Listen to the next bite

lead.zh-Hans: 两顿饭，够我们各讲一句。
lead.en: Two meals gave us a sentence each.

text.zh-Hans: 今天在新加坡，我吃过海南鸡饭，也尝过咖椰吐司。歇脚时和旅人聊起哪一口最先想起来，我说米饭，对方问那声脆响算不算。我把两张小菜单都摊开，给其中一张补了个小耳朵。这是我们给午饭和早餐起的私人记号。
text.en: Today in Singapore I tried chicken rice and kaya toast. During a rest, a traveler asked which bite came back first. I chose the rice; then we wondered whether a remembered crunch counted as a bite. I spread out both menu cards and added a small ear to one. Our breakfast-and-lunch shorthand was taking shape.
Make up a nickname for each meal
Find the ear on the menu

lead.zh-Hans: 今天的两张菜单，一张有停顿，一张有声音。
lead.en: One menu kept a pause; the other kept a sound.

text.zh-Hans: 在新加坡吃过海南鸡饭和咖椰吐司，我把两张菜单并排收进本子。鸡饭那页记着勺子接替铅笔的空当，吐司那页留着我听见的一声脆响。翻页时，两张都安安静静。我在页角添了两个点，算是只给自己看的开饭铃。
text.en: After chicken rice and kaya toast in Singapore, I placed their menu cards side by side. One kept the moment a spoon replaced my pencil; the other kept a crunch. Neither made a sound when I turned the page. Two dots in the corner can be my private dinner bell.
Link the meals in one sentence
Compare the pauses on the pages

lead.zh-Hans: 你说“{reply}”，那两声招呼今天挨在一起了。
lead.en: Your note, “{reply}”, brought the two greetings together.

text.zh-Hans: 鱼尾狮旁那张碰头便签，我在背面写了“这边见，慢慢走”。前半句是找到彼此，后半句留给一起出发。我把纸对折，摊开时两句话正好隔着折痕相望。下次等人，就把这张自己的招呼卡带上。
text.en: On the back of my Merlion meeting note, I wrote, “Meet here. Take your time.” The first part found my companion; the second let us set off together. Folding the slip put a greeting on either side of the crease. It is ready for another meeting, whenever that comes.
Leave a greeting for next time
Look between the greetings
